newsitem.title: FRANCE: Germany, France sign helicopter industrial deal.
newsitem.headline: Germany, France sign helicopter industrial deal.

text.p: French and German officials on Friday signed contracts to set up production lines to build the Franco-German Tiger combat helicopter.
The bilateral project has been plagued by cuts in French and German defence budgets as both countries struggle to cut public deficits in time to launch the single European currency by 1999.
Eurocopter, the Franco-German joint venture 70 percent held by French state-owned Aerospatiale and 30 percent by Daimler-Benz Aerospace AG (Dasa), will build the Tiger.
The contracts cover the helicopter airframe, the MTR 390 motor from the MTR group and anti-tank missile systems.
France is ordering an initial 80 ground support versions and Germany is buying the same number of anti-tank helicopters.

The French order is estimated at 12 billion francs, after a 10 percent price cut demanded by the DGA French procurement agency, Eurocopter chairman Francois Bigay had said. The DGA said that the cut resulted in a saving of 1.4 billion francs.
The order contracts are due in 1998, the DGA said.
The first deliveries are expected in 2002-2003.

The Tiger is a typical example of Franco-German defence industrial cooperation, involving an Aerospatiale-Dasa joint venture sharing development costs and production, with plants in both countries turning out aircraft to meet their respective armies' needs.

Aerospatiale had hoped to do similar joint ventures in missiles and space activities with Dasa, as part of an industrial consolidation, but saw its long-time German partner teaming instead with French rival Lagardere.
-- Pierre Tran, Le Bourget newsroom +33 1 4169 3649 pnt/bfl
